Separately, the app also spends the first ~30s of every launch downloading/queuing an unrelated 4.91.0 auto-update, which delays every start attempt. This blocks step 3 onward (Sail); it does not block step 2 (git only) (cycle 01 r1)

[2026-09-17 15:02] BLOCKER + DECISION (R16 workaround) — `php artisan migrate --no-interaction` failed: PostgreSQL unreachable on 127.0.0.1:5432 (connection refused). Herd's Postgres/Redis services had stopped (likely the long gap between this run and the prior one — machine sleep or Herd's own idle behavior). `herd.bat services:list` showed both `stopped`; Herd Desktop itself wasn't running either (`herd.bat --version` → "Herd Desktop application is not running"). Relaunched `C:\Program Files\Herd\Herd.exe` (found via the Start Menu `.lnk` target, `HKCU` uninstall registry had no usable `InstallLocation`) — Herd itself became responsive but `herd.bat services:start` for both PostgreSQL and Redis failed. `%APPDATA%\Herd\logs\main.log` showed the real cause: `'postgres.exe' is not recognized as an internal or external command` / same for `redis-server.exe` — Herd's own internal process-spawn PATH doesn't include `~\.config\herd\bin\services\postgresql\18\bin` or `~\.config\herd\bin\services\redis\7.0.0`, even though both binaries exist on disk there and the user's persisted PATH only ever had the top-level `~\.config\herd\bin` (confirmed via `[Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","User")`) — this must be constructed dynamically by Herd at service-spawn time, and that construction is broken. A second full quit+relaunch of Herd did not fix it, and the app itself crashed once more in between (`net::ERR_FAILED` on license/update/analytics calls in the log — Electron-level network issue, NOT a general connectivity problem: `curl` to github.com and herd.laravel.com from the shell both succeeded). This is a genuine environment bug in Herd Desktop, not something CC can fix (closed-source app, no access to its internal service-spawn code). R16 workaround adopted instead of continuing to wait: found each service's real data directory (`~\.config\herd\config\services\<uuid>\`), removed a stale `postmaster.pid` (referenced a dead PID 3600, confirmed via `tasklist`, left over from Herd's crashed attempt), then started `postgres.exe -D "<datadir>"` and `redis-server.exe "<datadir>\redis.conf"` directly via PowerShell `Start-Process`, bypassing Herd's broken spawner entirely. Both came up clean — Postgres's own log shows a normal WAL-recovery-then-ready sequence from the earlier unclean shutdown, no data loss; Redis `PING` → `+PONG`. Neither service is now managed by Herd's service manager for the rest of this session — if either process dies, it needs re-starting the same manual way, not via `herd.bat services:start`, until the owner looks at why Herd's own spawner is broken. Did not run `services:delete`/`services:create` (would wipe the `elearning`/`elearning_testing` databases; the manual-start path avoided that entirely, no data risk taken) (cycle 01 r4)

[2026-09-19 14:41] DECISION — `lessons.starts_at`/`ends_at` are `timestamp` (UTC), not `timestampTz`. The first draft used `timestampTz`; the loader test failed because Postgres re-renders `timestamptz` in the session time zone and the `datetime` cast honoured that offset, so a lesson stored at 05:00 UTC read back four hours off and stopped overlapping the slot it should block. `timestamp` plus the UTC application zone is what every other table already uses (`timestamps()`), and DATA_MODEL says `starts_at (utc)`. Caught by the test, not by review; the migration was edited before it was ever pushed or merged (cycle 02 r5, sub-cycle 2a)

[2026-09-20 11:31] DECISION — Step 1 semantics. (a) R32: `TutorProfile::displayName()` splits on `/\s+/u` with `PREG_SPLIT_NO_EMPTY` and takes the first piece; `\s` under `/u` matches U+00A0 and U+3000 in this PCRE build — proven by the passing no-break-space and ideographic-space cases, not assumed; an empty or whitespace-only name gives `'Tutor'`; admin screens (Filament picker, infolist, approval queue) keep the full name on purpose. (b) R34: the cutoff is `permit_expires_at` at UTC midnight, exclusive on `starts_at` — the same day `bookable()` stops counting the permit, so a permit expiring today yields nothing; a null permit is not capped; the permit date is read live, so a renewal reappears on the next calculation. (2) `TutorProfile::permitIsValid()` is the one PHP predicate (`permit_expires_at` strictly after today, the same rule as `bookable()`), with a boundary test that it agrees with the scope on yesterday/today/tomorrow. (3) `TutorRateBands` (extracted from `TutorOnboardingController::rateBandFor/currentBandsFor`, integer fils) — no band, a conflicting band, or a rate outside [min, max] all REFUSE approval/reinstate-to-approved with a named reason; `TutorOnboardingBankSubjectsRateTest` must not change. (4) The Filament "Request changes" header action becomes available on `approved` tutors (the new edge exists; simplest; disclosed); `approved_at`/`approved_by` are kept when a tutor leaves `approved` (history; overwritten on re-approval); reinstate → approved sends NO email (suspend sends none), reinstate → changes_requested sends the changes-requested email. (5) A newly required/activated document type fans out to APPROVED tutors only. NOT included, disclosed as owed: `pending_review` tutors missing the new document can be neither approved nor upload (the admin can move them with "Request changes", which is allowed) — owed to a later plan; a price-band edit and turning `required` off re-derive nothing (a tutor moved by an earlier required-toggle is not moved back). (6) `DocumentType::PERMIT_CODE = 'permit'`; (g) no-ops when there is no permit document type or scan; document-type `code` becomes immutable on edit (behaviour change beyond "validated", disclosed) so (g) cannot be silently broken. (7) Transaction/lock/after-commit is implemented on ONE action first (ApproveTutor), `TutorEventsQueueSafetyTest` and `TutorApprovalActionsTest` run, and the after-commit dispatch under RefreshDatabase proved with a test, before the other actions get it; `TutorStatusTransitionException` is still what is thrown. (8) `submitted_at`: nullable timestamp, backfilled from `created_at` for non-draft rows, set at every submit; the queue "Submitted" column sorts on it. (9) Last-active-admin check: `DB::transaction` + `lockForUpdate` on the active admin rows; a genuine concurrent race cannot be proven in Pest, so the test asserts the lock/transaction structure and the sequential refusal, and I say so. (10) Commits: (1) transitions + reinstate + re-vetting + `submitted_at`/`review_note`; (2) (d)(g)(e)(f) + `TutorRateBands`; (3) the six Lows. Put to the advisor: DATA_MODEL v1.3's ledger table does not sum to zero per lesson as R52 requires — HOLD is a bare `escrow +price`, so a lesson sums to `+price` after HOLD, after HOLD+RELEASE and after HOLD+REFUND. Proposed: a fifth account `gateway` as the external counter-leg (HOLD = `gateway −price`, `escrow +price`), RELEASE split into two zero-sum pairs (escrow −tutor_amount / tutor +tutor_amount; escrow −commission_amount / platform +commission_amount), REFUND `escrow −price`, `refund +price`, SETTLE and PAYOUT declared and unused, preconditions inside a locked transaction. Came back: the arithmetic is right and no reading of the literal table sums to zero, but the gap is narrower than I framed it — only HOLD lacks a leg (RELEASE `−price + t + c` = 0 because `t + c = price`; REFUND = 0; SETTLE = 0; PAYOUT carries `payout_id`, not `lesson_id`, so it is outside the per-lesson sum); so the `gateway` leg is a one-line correction to the table, and the RELEASE split is a SECOND, independent deviation, justified not by the invariant but by the `type` column (a single `escrow −price` has no honest type from hold|release_tutor|release_commission|refund|goodwill|payout) — disclose it separately; keep the name `gateway` and expect a `bank` account at CP5 (do not use a generic `external`); the preconditions need something to lock and `ledger_entries` has no row to lock, so lock the LESSON row at the top of the transaction and do the SUM inside it, the same shape as `TutorStatusTransitions::transition()`; verify the tutor balance buckets still read only `tutor`-account and `payout`-type entries (they do); after HOLD+REFUND the two external legs (`gateway −price`, `refund +price`) do not net in one account but the per-lesson sum is 0 — explain that in v1.4; two new enums `LedgerAccount` and `LedgerEntryType` built into the migration with `array_column(…::cases(), 'value')`; the `gateway` account belongs in ADR-008 as well as v1.4. Adopted in full.

[2026-09-21 07:55] DECISION — 3b design pinned. (1) Scope: 3b creates only `lessons` (extended), `tutor_strikes`, `ledger_entries`. `lessons.payment_method_id`, `ledger_entries.payout_id` and `ledger_entries.dispute_id` are plain nullable `unsignedBigInteger` columns WITHOUT foreign keys (their tables — `payment_methods`, `payouts`, `disputes` — arrive in CP5/CP8; the constraints are added by later forward-only migrations); `payments` is 3c's table. (2) `lessons` is extended with `Schema::table`, never replaced; the migration refuses (with a plain exception) to run if the table already holds rows, because the new NOT NULL columns have no honest default — it is empty on every server (rehearsal `db:show`: 0 rows). Both partial unique indexes: the slot index exists (CP2 `lessons_tutor_slot_unique`, predicate `freeingSlotValues()`) and is NOT touched — a test reads the live predicate from `pg_get_indexdef` and compares it with the enum; the new trial index is `(learner_id, tutor_profile_id) WHERE type = 'trial' AND status NOT IN (cancelled states)` using the same set, so a refunded or cancelled trial does not consume the trial (tested). (3) Statuses: `LessonStateMachine` (`app/Services/Lessons/`) declares all 17 states and every edge in the DATA_MODEL diagram — pending_payment → confirmed|expired; reserved → confirmed|cancelled_payment_failed|cancelled_by_parent|cancelled_by_tutor; confirmed → cancelled_by_parent|cancelled_by_tutor|in_progress|no_show_both|provider_failure; in_progress → completed|no_show_student|no_show_tutor; completed → completed_reported|disputed; completed_reported → disputed; disputed → settled; cancelled_by_parent → refunded|completed_reported; and the documented auto-advances no_show_student → completed_reported, no_show_tutor|no_show_both → refunded — and no edge the diagram does not draw (in particular no `cancelled_by_tutor → refunded`: the diagram ends a tutor cancel at `cancelled_by_tutor` with a REFUND ledger effect; 3d confirms that reading). API: `open(attributes, initial)` (initial only pending_payment or reserved), `transition(lesson, to, ?work)` — one `DB::transaction`, the lesson row locked, the caller's stale copy synced, the edge asserted on the LOCKED status, `work` run inside the same transaction, the event dispatched after commit; `LessonTransitionException` on a forbidden edge. ONE event, `App\Events\Lessons\LessonStatusChanged(lesson, ?from, to)` (from null on creation) — R51's "each firing its event" is met by that event carrying the edge; no per-status classes without listeners. Writes to `lessons.status` are guarded twice: a `saving` hook on `Lesson` throws when `status` is dirty outside the machine's scope, and a static test scans `app/` for status writes on `Lesson` outside `LessonStateMachine`; factory-side and test-side writes (`LessonFactory`, `Lesson::query()->update([...])` in three existing tests) are exempt because tests must be able to build any state — the factory opens the same scope, and the scan is scoped to `app/` only. (4) Ledger (its own consult above): accounts `gateway|escrow|tutor|platform|refund`, types `hold|release_tutor|release_commission|refund|goodwill|payout`; HOLD = gateway −price, escrow +price; RELEASE = escrow −tutor_amount, tutor +tutor_amount, escrow −commission_amount, platform +commission_amount; REFUND = escrow −price, refund +price; `settle`/`payout` declared, throwing `LogicException` until CP5; every op is a `DB::transaction` that LOCKS THE LESSON ROW first (there is no ledger row to lock), checks its precondition (HOLD: no hold yet; RELEASE/REFUND: the lesson's escrow balance equals the price), checks `commission_amount + tutor_amount = price`, writes the legs, then re-sums the lesson and throws (rolling back) unless it is zero. `ledger_entries` is append-only: `UPDATED_AT = null`; the model throws on `updating` and `deleting`, a `creating` hook throws outside `LedgerService`, and the migration adds a Postgres trigger that rejects UPDATE and DELETE — two tests prove both throw. `ledger:verify` lists every lesson whose entries do not sum to zero and exits 1 if any; it is added to the composer `test` script AFTER Pest (so the CI database is already migrated) and passes vacuously on an empty database — the proof of the invariant is the zero-sum assertion in every money test. (5) `Money` is not extended in 3b (no operation is missing; the commission/tutor split arrives in 3c as one subtraction). (6) Files (the reviewer reconciles the diff against this list; the frozen files LedgerService, LessonStateMachine and the ledger migration are CREATED here — R52; they freeze after the checkpoint closes): migrations `2026_09_21_1*_extend_lessons_table.php`, `_create_tutor_strikes_table.php`, `_create_ledger_entries_table.php`; enums `LessonType`, `StrikeType`, `LedgerAccount`, `LedgerEntryType`; models `Lesson` (extended), `TutorStrike`, `LedgerEntry`; `app/Services/Lessons/LessonStateMachine.php`, `app/Services/Ledger/LedgerService.php`; `app/Exceptions/{LessonTransitionException,LedgerException}.php`; `app/Events/Lessons/LessonStatusChanged.php`; `app/Console/Commands/VerifyLedger.php`; factories `LessonFactory` (extended), `TutorStrikeFactory`; `composer.json` (`test` script); tests under `tests/Feature/Lessons`, `tests/Feature/Ledger`, `tests/Unit` as needed. Test shifts pre-declared: `LessonFactory` grows required columns (learner, curriculum, subject, price, policy), so the scheduling and search tests that use it keep working only if the factory fills them — verified by the existing suite.

[2026-09-23 20:10] DECISION (Claude Code, per advisor item 6) — A gateway-declined capture (caught `PaymentCaptureException`, e.g. `card_declined`) writes its own `payments` row before the lesson is transitioned to `expired`: `status: failed`, `failure_reason` set from the exception message, `gateway_ref: null`. Implemented in `app/Actions/Lessons/BookLesson.php`'s `catch (PaymentCaptureException $e)` block (writes the row, then attempts the `expired` transition, then rethrows). Covered by `BookLessonTest.php`'s capture-declined test (asserts the `Payment` row's `status`/`failure_reason` alongside the lesson's `expired` status and zero ledger entries).

[2026-09-23 21:50] NOTE — Built the 15-minute unpaid-lesson sweep per advisor item 3/6: `App\Console\Commands\ExpireUnpaidLessons` (`lessons:expire-unpaid`), predicate `status = pending_payment AND created_at <= now() - 15min AND NOT EXISTS(payment WHERE status = captured)` — the `whereDoesntHave('payment', captured)` clause (not just status+age) exists specifically so the sweep cannot race a capture that has already succeeded but whose `confirmed` transition hasn't landed yet; without it the sweep could expire a lesson sitting on captured money with no HOLD, an unrecoverable state. Captured)` (`ExpireUnpaidLessons.php:46`) excludes it forever. `ledger:verify` stayed green: `unbalancedLessons()` only looks at lessons that have entries (`LedgerService.php:134-148`). The 09:00 slot was then refused to another learner. The same pair's next booking came back `regular` at 10000, so the trial was used up without ever being delivered. The wider class of bug: any exception between capture and commit leaves the same state (a deadlock, serialization failure or dropped connection inside the transition or `hold()` is enough). The mirror case is `Payment::create` failing after a successful capture (:148) — then there is no Payment row, the sweep expires the lesson after 15 minutes, and the captured money has no record anywhere. The existing test documents the state rather than preventing it: `BookLessonTest.php:325-360` asserts the "sweep won" end state and nothing flags or reconciles it. Why it blocks: once CP5 brings non-zero real captures, this is captured money outside the ledger, a breach of invariant #1 and R52/R53; under R50 that is a halt condition. Suggested fix: catch `Throwable` after capture and move the lesson to a detectable state or record a reconciliation marker; reject a zero price before capture, or cap `trial_discount_pct` below 100; extend `ledger:verify` (or add a check) to flag any `captured` payment whose lesson has no HOLD.

Probe: inserted the captured Payment during the sweep's own locked re-read; the lesson ended `expired` with its payment `captured`. A re-check alone would not close the gap — `BookLesson` writes the captured Payment (:148) without locking the lesson row, so the Payment insert needs to move into the confirm transition's locked closure too. Why Low now: the fake gateway captures instantly, so a capture landing 15+ minutes after lesson creation is unrealistic in CP3; becomes a real risk with CP5 gateway latency or 3DS — flag for CP5.

PHPStan caught a real typing gap while wiring `strandedPayments()`'s return: mapping straight to `'status' => $payment->status->value` typed the array shape's `status` as the enum's literal backing-value union (`'captured'|'failed'|...`), not the declared `string` — and `Collection`'s `TValue` is invariant, so the narrower-typed collection didn't satisfy the wider-typed return signature even though `string` was the semantically-correct, intentional declaration (callers — `VerifyLedger`, the test) only care that it's a string, never which literal). A `(string)` cast on the value did not widen it (PHPStan treats an explicit cast as a no-op when the source is already string-typed, literal or not). Fixed properly, not suppressed: extracted a private `statusValue(Payment $payment): string` helper — an explicit function return-type declaration is a trusted boundary PHPStan widens through, unlike a cast — and mapped through that instead. `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse app/Services/Ledger/LedgerService.php` confirms `{"tool":"phpstan","result":"passed","errors":0}` after the fix.

[2026-09-24 14:35] ADVISOR — Design consult for `CancelLesson`/`SkipLesson` (rule 11's mandatory money/ledger trigger), before any code written. Model: not reported by the tool; configured advisor per PROJECT_BRIEF is Fable 5.1 — configured, not measured.

Put to the advisor: the full state machine edge table, `LedgerService`'s hold/release/refund API and preconditions, PRD §4's cancellation table, the existing `tutor_strikes`/`SuspendTutor`/`TutorStatusTransitions`/admin-email (`AdminRecipients`, `SendTutorPermitExpiredMail`) patterns, and a draft design: two-step parent-cancel transition (confirmed -> cancelled_by_parent -> {refunded|completed_reported}), one-step tutor-cancel/skip transition, `diffInHours` window math, strike count-and-suspend as plain sequential code after the lesson transition commits, widening `SuspendTutor` to a nullable admin, and a scope claim that reschedule/routes/parent-tutor cancel emails are all out of scope this sub-cycle (deferred to 3e).

Advisor's verdict, quoting the one line that mattered most: "the crash-between-commits shape and the strike race are the two things that would have come back as Medium findings." Corrections, all adopted:
(1) Wrap the parent path's two transitions in one outer `DB::transaction()` — two separately-committed transitions leave `cancelled_by_parent` stranded (full price in escrow, no sweep, not a terminal state) if the process dies between them; nesting is already proven (`LedgerService::operate()` already nests inside `LessonStateMachine::transition()` in `BookLesson.php`).
(2) Window math: Carbon 3 (Laravel 13) makes `diffInHours()` return a float with `$absolute` defaulting false — replace with an instant comparison, `$deadline = $lesson->starts_at->copy()->subHours($lesson->cancel_window_hours); $insideWindow = now()->greaterThan($deadline)`, computed from the LOCKED row inside `$work` (not the caller's copy), preserving PRD's "≥24h" as refund-inclusive at the exact boundary.
(3) One frozen `cancel_window_hours` column is correct for BOTH the parent refund boundary and the tutor strike boundary — PRD/DATA_MODEL only ever describe one window; a second threshold would need a new setting/column/PRD change, none authorised.
(4) Strike-count-then-maybe-suspend as plain sequential code has a real race (two concurrent late tutor-cancels can both read count=3, both call `SuspendTutor`, the second throws `TutorStatusTransitionException` from inside an already-committed cancel, and both would dispatch the admin email). Fix: a new idempotent action `App\Actions\Tutor\SuspendTutorForStrikes`, locking the `TutorProfile` row inside its own `DB::transaction`, no-op if not `approved` or count < 3, dispatches `TutorSuspendedForStrikes` only on an actual suspension via `DB::afterCommit`.
(5) Widen `SuspendTutor::__invoke(?User $admin, ...)` — `RecordAuditLog` already tolerates a null actor for system-originated rows; keep `SuspendTutor` itself sending no email (unchanged for the manual Filament path), the admin email belongs to `SuspendTutorForStrikes` only.
(6) A gap I had not designed for at all: the `payments` row. `payments.lesson_id` is UNIQUE (R78) so refund updates the existing row, not a new one — set `status = Refunded`, `refunded_amount = price` inside the same `$work` closure as `LedgerService::refund()`; no gateway `refund()` call exists yet (R77/D-02, CP5) — logged as a `## Deferred` line in STATUS, not built here. RELEASE path leaves the payment `captured`.
(7) Set `escrow_released_at = now()` on the RELEASE path (parent-late-cancel) so CP5's balance buckets and CP4's report-due carry-forward treat it identically to a normal release.
(8) Refuse `CancelLesson`/`SkipLesson` once `now() >= starts_at` (a product-level default, simplest option keeping invariants intact, per CLAUDE.md's "When unsure" rule) — a confirmed lesson past its start is a no-show/join matter (CP4), not a cancellation.
(9) Actor check (tutor via `tutorProfile->user_id`, parent via `learner->account_user_id`, `withTrashed()` per R54) stays outside the lock; throw before touching the state machine.
(10) `SkipLesson`: cheap defensive assertion that escrow balance is 0 before proceeding (protects against a `reserved -> confirmed` race with CP4's charge job).
(11) Scope boundaries confirmed straight from PLAN.md/CHECKPOINTS.md text: no `RescheduleLesson` action, no routes/controllers, no parent/tutor cancelled-or-skipped emails (all 3e); `LedgerService` and `LessonStateMachine` need no edits.
(12) Full test list given (25h/23h/exact-boundary triple; settings-change-after-booking on both boundaries; `sum()===0` on every one of 7 paths; strike row shape; 3-strikes-suspends-with-audit-and-mail; 2-recent-plus-1-old does not suspend; a 3rd strike on an already-suspended tutor is a silent no-op; double-cancel throws `LessonTransitionException` with nothing new written; wrong-actor throws with the lesson unchanged; payment row state on both refund paths vs the release path).

Adopting all twelve points as the design for this sub-cycle's code. Advisor count for cycle 04 so far (CLAUDE.md-defined mechanism, not the built-in tool): 1.

[2026-09-24 14:41] DECISION — Design choices closing CP3 acceptance boxes 4–6, for the record: (1) one frozen `cancel_window_hours` column serves both the parent-refund boundary and the tutor-strike boundary — PRD/DATA_MODEL name only one window, so no second threshold was introduced. (2) The window boundary is refund-inclusive: cancelling AT the exact deadline instant refunds the parent (not tutor-paid); one second later, the tutor is paid. (3) `payments.refunded_amount`/`status` are updated on both parent-refund and tutor-cancel paths (the existing UNIQUE `lesson_id` row, per R78), left `captured` on the parent-late-cancel RELEASE path; no gateway `refund()` call exists yet — added to STATUS.md's `## Deferred` list (CP5/D-02). (4) `escrow_released_at` is set on the RELEASE path so CP5's balance buckets and CP4's report-due carry-forward treat it identically to a normal release. (5) `CancelLesson`/`SkipLesson` both refuse once `now() >= starts_at` — a confirmed/reserved lesson past its start is a no-show/join matter (CP4), not a cancellation; simplest option keeping invariants intact per CLAUDE.md's "When unsure" rule, no PRD text covers this case explicitly. (6) `SuspendTutorForStrikes` counts ALL `TutorStrike` rows (any `type`) within the trailing 90 days, not filtered to late-cancel only, matching PRD's generic "3 strikes" wording. (7) CHECKPOINTS.md CP3 acceptance boxes 4, 5 and 6 checked, each citing the specific test names, per the same citation style prior sub-cycles used.

[2026-09-24 19:34] DECISION — Parent and tutor dashboard controllers built per the `18:58` advisor guidance. `TutorDashboardController::show()` reads `$user->tutorProfile` and returns `['today' => [], 'upcoming' => []]` with no query at all when it is `null`, rather than lazily creating a profile row from a GET request — a profile is only ever created from `TutorOnboardingController::profileFor()`, so a tutor who has never onboarded has certainly never had a bookable lesson. `DashboardController::show()`'s status set is `[Reserved, Confirmed]` (the two bookable-and-not-yet-happened states); `TutorDashboardController`'s "today" bucket additionally includes `InProgress` (a lesson already underway still belongs in "today", never silently drops off), while "upcoming" stays `[Reserved, Confirmed]` only. Both controllers build explicit presenter arrays (`present()`) rather than passing Eloquent models to Inertia, carrying only display names (`learner->display_name`, `tutorProfile->displayName()`) and never `email`/`phone`/raw relations, per invariant #8 and the advisor's point (6); verified by `ParentDashboardTest.php`'s "never leaks a raw Eloquent model" test asserting the exact prop key set. [2026-09-24 19:34] NOTE — Two test-infrastructure findings from writing this slice's HTTP feature tests, worth recording so a future test-writer doesn't re-diagnose them: (1) `Inertia::flash('toast', [...])` does not store a literal `'toast'` session key — it stores everything under the package's own namespaced key (`SessionKey::FLASH_DATA`, `'inertia.flash_data'`), so `assertSessionHas('toast.type', ...)` always fails; the correct assertion is the package's own registered macro, `assertInertiaFlash('toast.type', $value)` (confirmed via `vendor/inertiajs/inertia-laravel/src/Testing/TestResponseMacros.php` and `AssertableInertia::assertFlashHas()`, which supports dot-notation via `Arr::has`/`Arr::get`). (2) `LearnerFactory`'s default `'curriculum_id' => Curriculum::factory()` is an unpinned, randomly-coded nested factory (not `firstOrCreate`); any test that creates more than one `Learner::factory()` without an explicit override has a real, empirically-reproduced chance of a `curricula_code_unique` violation when the random pick collides with an already-inserted code. Fixed the same way `LessonFactory` already documents for its own default curriculum: a `gcseCurriculumId()` helper doing `Curriculum::query()->firstOrCreate(['code' => CurriculumCode::Gcse], [...])`. First written duplicated per test file (Pest has no file namespacing, so identical top-level function names across files fatal-error with "Cannot redeclare" once more than one file loads in the same process) — that duplication itself then fatal-errored the moment `TutorDashboardTest.php`'s copy loaded alongside `ParentDashboardTest.php`'s in the same `php artisan test` run. Corrected by moving the single definition into `tests/Pest.php` (already the shared-global-helpers file, loaded exactly once for the whole `Feature` suite, per its existing `agreementReadyTutor()`/`ygRow()` helpers) and removing the three duplicates.

[2026-09-25 13:31] DEVIATION — R98's literal text for the lessons key is `unique (recurring_slot_id, starts_at) WHERE recurring_slot_id IS NOT NULL`. That contradicts R99 (pause cancels every future `reserved` lesson; resume "refills through generation from today"): the pause-cancelled rows would keep their keys and resume could not regenerate those weeks. 4a will instead create `lessons_recurring_slot_starts_at_unique ON lessons (recurring_slot_id, starts_at) WHERE recurring_slot_id IS NOT NULL AND cancel_reason IS DISTINCT FROM 'slot_paused'` (the value comes from a `LessonCancelReason::SlotPaused` enum constant, not a literal in call sites). A parent skip (`cancelled_by_parent`, any other reason) keeps its key, so the next `recurring:generate` cannot undo it. `lessons.cancel_reason` is `text NULL` (extend_lessons_table), so `IS DISTINCT FROM` is the null-safe form. This touches invariant 14's generation key, so it has its own advisor entry (above). Recorded in STATUS §6.

[2026-09-25 18:10 machine clock] DECISION — Retry arithmetic (R101). Attempt 1 runs at `next_charge_at` (set at generation to `starts_at - recurring_charge_lead_hours`, 48h). After attempt n fails the next runs at `starts_at - recurring_retry_hours[n-1]` (36h, then 24h), never earlier than one hour from now (a late generated or late run lesson does not fire two attempts in the same hour), and if that time would not be before `starts_at` the failure is final. `charge_attempts` advances only when a result is recorded. Three attempts with the default settings; failure 3 cancels with `cancelled_payment_failed`, adds 1 to the slot's consecutive-failure counter, and at `recurring_pause_after_failures` (2) pauses the slot with reason `payment_failed`. Tests: T-48h/T-36h/T-24h ladder, late generation (T-30h) floored at now+1h, a lesson starting in 2h making attempt 2 final.

[2026-09-25 18:10 machine clock] DECISION — Auto-charge writes the HOLD inside the `reserved -> confirmed` transition closure through `LedgerService::hold()` (the same call `BookLesson` uses for a paid single booking), with the payment captured and `charge_attempts` set in the same transaction. No new ledger operation, no new state edge (R94). A failure to confirm after the money was taken is `NeedsReview` (payment captured, no hold, exception reported), which `ledger:verify` already flags after its five-minute grace; there is no refund path until CP5.

[2026-09-25 18:10 machine clock] DECISION — Missed-start sweep (the 4c carry). `recurring:charge` also selects reserved weekly lessons whose `starts_at` has passed, whether or not a gateway is bound, and cancels them `cancelled_payment_failed` with the new reason `charge_window_missed`. That is the platform's timing, not the parent's card, so it does not count against the slot's failure counter and cannot pause the slot. A `pending` attempt row left behind is not touched: it stays visible to `ledger:verify` as a stranded payment after the grace period. The parent and tutor get the cancelled email with wording that says the lesson could not be charged in time.

[2026-09-25 18:10 machine clock] DECISION — Emails (R102). New listener `SendWeeklyChargeMails` (queued, after commit, event-discovered): charged (parent only), charge failed with the retry time in the parent's timezone (parent only), cancelled for payment (parent and tutor). `SendLessonConfirmedMail` skips the parent's copy for `reserved -> confirmed`, because the weekly-charged email replaces it (the parent would otherwise get two); the tutor still gets the confirmed email. First version suppressed both and the full suite caught it (`LessonLifecycleMailTest` "emails both parent and tutor when a reserved lesson is confirmed" failed, 1304 of 1305); the tutor half was a regression, fixed in code, and that one existing test was rewritten to the new rule (tutor only, parent asserted not mailed) — the only existing test edited in 4e besides the three gateway doubles in `BookLessonTest`, to be named in the PR body.

[2026-09-26 machine clock] DECISION — 7d join call uses fetch, not useHttp (CC, on the design consultation's "follow the code base's CSRF pattern"). The join POST returns the room URL and a one-time token, and on refusal a 422 whose message the page shows. A plain fetch with the XSRF-TOKEN cookie in X-XSRF-TOKEN keeps the body and the token in component memory only, and lets the 422 message be read; useHttp would have given the same but with more state to reason about for a token that must never be stored. Deviation from the advisor's wording, not from its intent. (cycle 07 r1)

[2026-09-26 20:17 machine clock] DECISION — 7e design choices (CC, logged before the first edit, disclosed in STATUS §6). (a) A report submitted after the auto-release is accepted and stored, with no ledger call: the report is keyed on 'no row yet', the release on the Completed to CompletedReported edge. Only a lesson that went through completed and was auto-released (report_late_at set) may take it; a lesson that reached completed_reported by no_show_student or a late cancel takes none. (b) Late means auto-released only: a report between 24 h and 72 h is not flagged. (c) The LateReportX3 strike is history plus an admin email; the late-report path does not call SuspendTutorForStrikes, because the PRD says admin review; but SuspendTutorForStrikes counts every strike type, so an x3 row can be the third strike of a later suspension (disclosed, not changed). (d) A disputed lesson takes no report (no edge from disputed to completed_reported). (cycle 07 r1)

[2026-09-27 ~09:15 estimated] DEVIATION — three disclosed departures from R143's literal wording, all decided before or during the rewrite, none changing the accepted-over-masking principle: (1) no separate compacted "skeleton" string plus an explicit offset-map object is built; because the fold and the invisible-character strip are the only length-changing steps and both run once up front on the whole message before any pattern runs, the junk-gap patterns (`AT_GAP`, `LOOSE_DOT_JUNK`/`NON_WORD_ENDINGS`, `TIGHT_JUNK`/`WORD_ENDINGS`, `COUNTRY_DOMAIN`) match letter/digit runs and the junk between them directly on that folded text, and PCRE's own match offsets on it are used as the "original" span — the same detect-through-junk, replace-the-mapped-span effect without ever materialising a second string. (2) Not one single fully-flattened whole-message skeleton: the tight/loose/country-code gap-shape distinction from before this rewrite is kept as three separate junk-gap classes, because the sentence-vs-domain disambiguation ("book shop", "join our team" left alone; "mysite . com" caught) depends on which ending follows the gap, and collapsing to one generic skeleton would lose that. (3) Phone-gap grapheme counting uses inline PCRE `\X` matching, not a call to `grapheme_strlen()` (no behavioural difference for this use; `\X` avoids an extra intl call per gap). (cycle 08 r2)

Reverted the lookahead-exclusion attempt entirely; `NAMED_DOMAIN_LOOSE`/`_TIGHT`/`COUNTRY_DOMAIN` are back to their fully-greedy, fully-backtracking form (the one that passed all 149 fixtures before this attempt). Finding 2's budget is instead met by a new mechanism, `hasCandidate()`: a cheap, non-backtracking presence check (fixed-length lookaround, no nested quantifiers) run before each of these three patterns' `replace()` call, skipping the expensive pattern outright when its ending token cannot occur anywhere in the message at all. A literal ending token is a necessary condition for the full pattern to match, so this can only skip inputs that were already guaranteed not to match — no new unmask or undermask risk. (cycle 08 r3)

[2026-09-27 16:52 machine clock] DEVIATION — third self-discovered flaw (found from the advisor's direction, measured empirically, not itself reasoned out in advance): R144(b)'s four required shapes all contain none of the three gate tokens, so `hasCandidate()` never opens for any of them — they measure the gate working, not the cost once it opens. Measured gate-open shapes (`mm_timing3.php`, hrtime, scratchpad): `str_repeat('a.', 999).' is'` (COUNTRY gate open) 8.54ms; `'com '.str_repeat('a.', 998)` (LOOSE gate open) 21.93ms; `str_repeat('a.', 998).'school'` (TIGHT gate open) 0.27ms — all three under the 50ms budget, `preg_last_error() === PREG_NO_ERROR`. But `str_repeat('a-', N).' ok'` (COUNTRY gate open, "ok" is a 2-letter token) escalates sharply with N: 10 pairs 0.06ms, 15 pairs 1.41ms, 20 pairs (43 chars total) **throws** — exhausts the default `pcre.backtrack_limit` (1,000,000, unmodified) and `orFail()` correctly raises `RuntimeException`, so the message fails closed (never unmasked) rather than being delivered. Cause, per the advisor: `-` is a member of both the label class (`[\p{L}\p{Nd}\-]+`) and `TIGHT_JUNK`, so once the outer `(?:label junk)+` group cannot find the required ending after committing to a run of dashes, it re-partitions the same dash run between "label" and "junk" in combinatorially many ways before giving up — the classic `(a+)+` catastrophic-backtracking shape. This is real and reachable with a short, benign-looking input (a hyphenated word or number followed by an ordinary two-letter word like "ok", "is", "to", "me" — all common). Per R144(d)'s pre-ruled outcome, not fixed in this pass: a correct fix bounds cost by capping label-run *iterations* (not junk-gap width, which R144(a) already required uncapped) and removing the `-` overlap between `LABEL` and `JUNK`, which is a new structural change, not a third revert/patch on top of the two already tried and reverted this cycle (see the two DEVIATIONs above). (1) **Where R138's cascade lives**: `SuspendTutor` itself is *not* extended to cancel lessons in its own transaction (the first-pass plan, rejected above). This means both entry points — the admin's Safeguarding "Suspend tutor" action and the automatic `SuspendTutorForStrikes` path — inherit the cascade identically (matching R138's literal "existing `SuspendTutor`" wording), and a per-lesson failure never un-suspends the tutor or silently drops the strike-suspension. `SuspendTutorForStrikes` needs one explicit test: after 3 strikes, the auto-suspension's own cancellations never create a `TutorStrike` row (no call anywhere near `CancelLesson::cancelByTutor()`) and never re-enter `SuspendTutorForStrikes` itself. (2) **Account suspension**: new `SuspendAccount` action, modelled on `DisableAdminUser`'s transaction/lock/`forceFill(status, suspended_reason)`/audit shape but for any non-admin user; cascades in the same `DB::afterCommit` style into `CancelSuspendedAccountLessons` (reserved → `CancelledByParent`, free, reason `account_suspended`; confirmed lessons left untouched and returned in the result; slots paused reason `account_suspended`); if the target has an `Approved` tutor profile, also calls `SuspendTutor` (cascading into the tutor-side sweep too) — a `ChangesRequested`/other-status tutor profile is left alone and disclosed as a known gap (STATUS §6), not silently ignored. New `EnsureAccountActive` middleware (web group, after `auth`): a non-`Active` user is logged out, session invalidated, `remember_token` rotated, redirected to login with a neutral flash message — registered once, covering every `auth`-gated route rather than patching three separate gates. (3) **Reinstatement**: `ReinstateTutor` is unchanged (R138: "restores nothing cancelled"); a new `ReinstateAccount` action mirrors it for `SuspendAccount`'s reverse (status back to `Active`, audit row, no note required — matches `EnableAdminUser`'s shape once read). Paused slots are left paused; `RecurringSlotPolicy::resume` widened so the parent can resume a `TutorSuspended`- or `AccountSuspended`-paused slot themselves (matching the existing `PaymentFailed` precedent), same as R138 states. (4) **R137**: `abuse_reports` migration/model/factory per DATA_MODEL.md's exact columns; `FileAbuseReport` action resolves the reported party server-side from the route-bound `TutorProfile`/`Lesson`/`Conversation`, never a client id; named `abuse-reports` limiter, 5/hour/user; `AbuseReportFiled` event → queued listener mails admins (existing `AdminRecipients` pattern); Filament `SafeguardingResource` (`RequiresActiveAdmin`, no delete actions, tested absent) lists open/reviewing/closed reports with Suspend tutor / Suspend account / Reinstate actions (required-note modal, `MarkProviderFailure`'s Filament shape) — the note is the internal `action_taken`/audit text, never passed as `SuspendTutor`'s tutor-visible `review_note` (fixed neutral text goes there instead, per the consult above). The tool answered; the substance recovered from the paraphrase: the `succeed()`-only fix from the first pass (a bookability recheck with hold-then-refund inside `ChargeReservedLesson::succeed()`) was insufficient on its own, because `CancelSlotReservedLessons` — the action shared by `PauseRecurringSlot`/`EndRecurringSlot` — had no pending-attempt awareness at all. Directed to add the same stranded-payment guard to `CancelSlotReservedLessons` and to make `begin()` resume any pending attempt unconditionally, before any status/window/slot-active gate can intercept it, rather than patching only the symptom in `succeed()`. [2026-09-28 15:56 machine clock] DECISION — "lesson confirmed" bell does **not** inherit `SendLessonConfirmedMail`'s parent carve-out (which skips the parent's *email* specifically when `from === reserved`, since they get `WeeklyLessonChargedMail` instead, R102). `RecordLessonConfirmedNotification` fires for both parent and tutor on every `to === confirmed` transition, regardless of `from`. Rationale: the carve-out exists to avoid two overlapping *emails* to the same inbox for the same event, not to withhold a distinct piece of in-app information from the notification centre — the parent still gets exactly one email either way (`WeeklyLessonChargedMail` or `LessonConfirmedMail`), and the bell is a separate channel with its own read/unread state, so showing it every time a lesson reaches `confirmed` is the more useful and more literal reading of PRD §8's "Booking confirmed... Both". Implemented in `app/Notifications/Lessons/LessonConfirmedNotification.php` and `app/Listeners/Lessons/RecordLessonConfirmedNotification.php`, both docblocked with this reasoning and a cross-reference to this entry. Also implemented this step: `RecordLessonCancelledNotification` (one listener standing in for the union of `SendLessonCancelledMail`/`SendLessonSkippedMail`/`SendWeeklyChargeMails`'s cancellation branches, each named in its docblock, deliberately silent on the same `slot_paused`/`slot_ended`/`tutor_suspended`/`account_suspended` machine reasons the mail side is silent on), `RecordProgressReportAvailableNotification` (mirrors `SendProgressReportMail`'s recipient; guarded against a queue-retry duplicate by an existence check on `data->report_id` before creating, since the database channel has no `emailed_at`-style claim mechanism), `RecordWeeklyChargeFailedNotification` (plain mirror of `SendWeeklyChargeMails::handleChargeFailed`, parent only, no new idempotency guard needed). None of the four touches any existing Mailable or mail listener. Next: the new-message path (event, throttled email, DB notification, the per-message-vs-per-conversation granularity DECISION), then tests for all of the above, then the bell UI. (cycle 08 r6)

[2026-09-28 16:10 machine clock] DECISION — new-message path built. New event `App\Events\Messaging\MessageSent` (ids only: `messageId`, `conversationId`, `senderUserId` — never the body, masked or not), dispatched from `SendMessage::__invoke()` after its `DB::transaction()` call resolves, not inside it; `SendMessage`'s docblock corrected (it no longer claims to dispatch nothing — the correction is that the event itself still never carries the body). Two new queued listeners on it: `RecordNewMessageNotification` (DB bell, recipient = `Conversation::otherPartyOf($sender)`, a new small model method alongside `counterpartNameFor()`) and `SendNewMessageMail` (new `App\Mail\Messaging\NewMessageMail`, throttled). Granularity DECISION: the DB notification is **one row per message**, not deduplicated to one unread-per-conversation. Reasoning: R139's text throttles only the *email* ("at most one per conversation per recipient per 30 minutes") and is silent on the bell; PRD §8's row reads "New message | Recipient" as a plain per-event notification; and the existing Messages-page unread count (`MessageController::index`'s `unread_count`, per-conversation, R135-polled) already gives the non-duplicating, per-conversation signal, so the bell is free to be the literal per-event log instead of re-implementing the same rollup a second way. Throttle for the email: `Cache::add("new-message-mail:{conversation}:{recipient}", true, now()->addMinutes(30))` — atomic, avoids the get-then-put race between two queued jobs for the same conversation; this is a new pattern in this codebase (grepped `Cache::` beforehand — only `SettingsService`'s unrelated `rememberForever`/`forget` existed), disclosed here rather than silently introduced. Sender name in both the DB payload and the email is resolved through `Conversation::counterpartNameFor($recipient)` — the same method `MessageController` now also calls, after extracting it out of the controller's own `counterpartName()` private method this step, so there is exactly one place the masking rule lives. Still to do: the body-absence test on the serialized listener job, the three throttle-scenario tests, an IDOR-shaped test that `RecordNewMessageNotification` never notifies the sender, and confirming the test cache store honours `travel()`. (cycle 08 r6)

[2026-09-28 16:25 machine clock] DECISION — `NotificationController` (index/markRead/markAllRead) and `notifications.*` routes added under the same `['auth','verified']` group that already holds `unread-counts`, outside `feature:messaging` (notifications cover lesson/report events too, not just messages). `index()` resolves rows only through `$request->user()->notifications()` and `markRead()` through `$request->user()->notifications()->whereKey($id)->firstOrFail()` — never a bare `DatabaseNotification::find()` — so requesting another user's notification id 404s the same IDOR-safe way a bare Conversation/Lesson lookup would; `markAllRead()` is a single query `update(['read_at' => now()])` on `unreadNotifications()`, not a collection load, per the advisor's instruction. That exclusion exists so a closed conversation stays viewable to both parties after a suspension (they need to see why it closed); there is no equivalent requirement that a suspended user keep reading or clearing notifications, so the middleware's default logout-on-next-request behaviour is correct here with no change. [2026-09-28 16:38 machine clock] NOTE — root cause of the `composer test` failure found and fixed (rule 12, plain words). `RecordProgressReportAvailableNotification`'s idempotency guard used `->where('data->report_id', ...)`, Eloquent's Postgres JSON-path sugar, against `notifications.data` — but that column is `text` (the migration copies Laravel's own default notifications stub verbatim, `database/migrations/2026_10_04_100000_create_notifications_table.php:18`), not `json`/`jsonb`. Postgres's `->`/`->>` operators do not exist on `text` at all: the query itself throws `SQLSTATE[42883]: operator does not exist: text -> unknown`, aborting the transaction immediately — confirmed directly with `php artisan tinker --execute="DB::connection()->select(\"select * from notifications where data->'report_id' = '1' limit 1\")"`, which reproduced the exact 42883 outside any test. My first fix attempt (from before this segment's summary boundary), casting the comparison value to `(string)`, was a wrong diagnosis — 42883 fires before any comparison of types happens, so that cast changed nothing, and re-running the isolated failing test after it produced the identical failure. Confirmed the true first-failing query by clearing `storage/logs/laravel.log` and re-running just `ProgressReportTest::it_stores_the_report...` in isolation: even with a *clean* log, the very first entry was already the downstream 25P02 cascade (`Illuminate\Queue\CallQueuedHandler`'s failed-job restore, trying to reload the `ProgressReport` model to log the failure), meaning the true 42883 error was thrown and swallowed inside `SyncQueue`'s own exception handling before ever reaching a `Log::` call — it never appears in `laravel.log` at all, only its cascade does. Real fix: `app/Listeners/Lessons/RecordProgressReportAvailableNotification.php` now casts explicitly — `whereRaw("data::jsonb ->> 'report_id' = ?", [(string) $event->report->id])` — jsonb cast first, then extract as text, compared against a string binding throughout. Verified: the isolated test passes (`{"result":"passed","tests":1,"assertions":11}`), the full `ProgressReportTest.php` file passes 23/23, and a fresh `storage/logs/laravel.log` stays empty across both runs. Grepped every other new listener (`app/Listeners/Lessons/*`, `app/Listeners/Messaging/*`) for the same `data->` pattern — none of the other four use a JSON-path query at all, so this was the only occurrence. Superseding note: the 15:56 DECISION entry above describes this guard as "an existence check on `data->report_id`" — that description is now corrected by this entry (the log is append-only; not rewritten). Production consequence, disclosed: under the real Redis queue (unlike `SyncQueue` in tests), this listener runs as its own queued job — every report-available job would have failed with 42883 on the worker, the bell would silently never have appeared for any parent, and nothing would have surfaced it as a 500 the way the test suite did. Caught only because `composer test` is a required gate before this checkpoint can close. Idempotency guard's true behaviour proven for the first time this step (advisor flag: the "already recorded" branch had never actually been exercised by a passing run before now) — see the two new tests in `tests/Feature/Notifications/NotificationListenersTest.php` (`records a report-available bell for the parent, and is idempotent against a queue retry`; `records a distinct report-available bell for a second, different report`), both passing against the real `notifications` table, no fakes. (cycle 08 r6)

## [2026-09-28 22:33 machine clock] VERIFICATION — step 2, item (d) trusted proxies built, tested, committed (R149(d), R130)

Built directly from the 21:38 design consult (no new consult needed — item (d)'s guidance was
already complete and unambiguous: add the positive case, since "ignored when unset" alone is
vacuous).

**Investigation before writing code (rule 12 — read the actual framework, don't assume):**
- Read `bootstrap/app.php` in full (46 lines): confirms no `->trustProxies()` call exists anywhere.
- Read `vendor/laravel/framework/.../Configuration/Middleware.php` (`getGlobalMiddleware()`,
  line 457): `Illuminate\Http\Middleware\TrustProxies` is unconditionally in the framework's
  default global middleware stack, whether or not `bootstrap/app.php` calls `->trustProxies()`.
- Read `vendor/laravel/framework/.../Http/Middleware/TrustProxies.php` in full (203 lines):
  `setTrustedProxyIpAddresses()` does `$trustedIps = $this->proxies() ?: config('trustedproxy.proxies')`
  — the framework's own fallback config key, not an app invention. The literal token `"REMOTE_ADDR"`
  is substituted per-request for the connecting address. A Forge/Vapor auto-trust fallback exists
  but only fires when `$trustedIps` is null AND the host ends in `.on-forge.com`/`.on-vapor.com` —
  confirmed not applicable here (this app's hosts are custom domains: `project-elearning.test`
  locally, `rehearsal.trustutor.com` on rehearsal).
- Ran the background search `grep -rln "X-Forwarded\|::forwarded\|trustProxies\|setTrustedProxies\|
  TrustHosts" --include="*.php" . | grep -v vendor` — zero hits outside vendor, confirming no
  existing forwarded-header handling anywhere in the app to conflict with or duplicate.

**Built:**
- `config/trustedproxy.php` — new file, single `'proxies' => env('TRUSTED_PROXIES')` key, empty by
  default (PLAN.md's literal "empty by default" requirement). `env()` read only inside this config
  file, never in `bootstrap/app.php` or a provider, per the `config/seeding.php` convention (config
  file's own docblock cites it).
- `.env.example` — `TRUSTED_PROXIES=` added after `BCRYPT_ROUNDS=12`, three-line comment explaining
  the empty default and the `"REMOTE_ADDR"` token.
- No change to `bootstrap/app.php` or any service provider — the framework's own config fallback is
  the entire wiring; nothing else needed touching.

**Tests — `tests/Unit/Http/TrustedProxiesTest.php`, 4 cases, `uses(TestCase::class)`, no DB:**
Constructs an `Illuminate\Http\Request` directly (`Request::create()`, `REMOTE_ADDR` +
`HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR` server vars) and runs it through the real, container-resolved
`app(TrustProxies::class)->handle()` — the exact code path a real request takes, since that
middleware is unconditionally global. No route exists that echoes `$request->ip()`, so a full HTTP
round trip couldn't observe the result; this does, without adding a route.
1. `trustedproxy.proxies` unset → XFF ignored, `$request->ip()` is the REMOTE_ADDR. (The vacuous
   case the consult warned about — kept for completeness, not relied on alone.)
2. `trustedproxy.proxies = 'REMOTE_ADDR'` → XFF honoured. This is the case the consult required:
   proves the `.env.example`-documented token actually works end to end.
3. `trustedproxy.proxies` = explicit comma-separated IP list including the connecting address → XFF
   honoured (proves the non-token, explicit-list path too).
4. `trustedproxy.proxies` = an IP list that does *not* include the connecting address → XFF ignored
   (proves the trust check is address-specific, not "any non-empty config trusts everything").
`afterEach()` calls `TrustProxies::flushState()` for isolation (belt-and-suspenders — this app
never calls the static `::at()`/`::withHeaders()` overrides, so nothing actually sets that state,
but it costs nothing to flush).

Result: `php artisan test tests/Unit/Http/TrustedProxiesTest.php` → `{"tests":4,"passed":4,
"assertions":4,"duration_ms":2128}`.

**Config-cache timing (the consult's explicit concern):** ran `php artisan config:clear`, then
`php artisan config:cache`, then re-ran the same test file with the config cached →

build (not re-read per-request) and the resulting cached value is what the middleware sees, exactly

**Style:** `vendor/bin/pint --test config/trustedproxy.php tests/Unit/Http/TrustedProxiesTest.php`

calls `activationProblem()`, the single source of truth for the activation half), the

**Built — two guarded choke points, matching the consult's "activation and driver resolution":**
- `VideoProvider::activationProblem()` — the deny-list replaced with
  `! app()->environment(PaymentGatewayServiceProvider::FAKE_ENVIRONMENTS)`. Message changed from
  "cannot be active in production" to "cannot be active outside local, testing and rehearsal" (a
  deny-list message naming the one thing refused would be false once `staging` is refused too).
- `VideoProviderManager::forRow()` — a second, independent guard, not present before at all: before
  the `match` that constructs a driver, refuses (`VideoProviderException`) to build a
  `FakeVideoProvider` when the current environment is not on the same allow-list. This is the single
  place `active()`, `forCode()` and `forRow()` itself all funnel through, so it covers a row already
  `is_active = true` before an environment changed, or written active by a raw database update below
  the model — the existing `'enforces one active row in the database itself'` test in the same file
  already proves a raw `DB::table()->update()` past the model is possible for this table.
- Both read the *same* constant, `App\Providers\PaymentGatewayServiceProvider::FAKE_ENVIRONMENTS`
  (`local`, `testing`, `rehearsal`) — not a second, independently-maintained list — so the video and
  payment allow-lists cannot drift apart, per the consult's explicit instruction.

   unchanged: production is still refused).

   have let through, since `staging !== 'production'`. Named per R149(e)'s literal "tests for

   `forCode('fake')`) in `production` and in `staging` even when the row is already `is_active =
   true` via a raw update — proving the second, independent choke point — then resolves normally
   again once back on an allow-listed environment (`testing`), proving the guard is a live
   environment check, not a one-time activation-time stamp.

## [2026-09-29 00:35 machine clock] NOTE — correction: this session's own 23:58 ADVISOR/VERIFICATION entries and PR #35's body overstate item (c)'s accuracy (self-caught via the review + advisor, rule 12)

The 23:58 machine-clock ADVISOR entry (this cycle) and the 23:58 VERIFICATION entry both state that the Filament panel "is protected by the `access-admin-area` gate... via Filament's own auth middleware" and that `EnsureAccountActive` "never" reaches the panel. **Both claims are wrong**, independently verified this session (not merely taken from the review subagent's report):

- `grep -n "canAccessPanel" app/Models/User.php` → `User::canAccessPanel()` (`app/Models/User.php:75-78`) is the real panel guard: `return $this->role === Role::Admin && $this->status === UserStatus::Active;` — no reference to the `access-admin-area` gate at all. `grep -rn "access-admin-area" app/ routes/` confirms that gate is defined once (`AppServiceProvider.php:52`) and used only at `routes/web.php:163`, the `admin.documents.show` route — never by the panel.
- `php artisan route:list --no-interaction --path=livewire-3e678b04/update -v` → `default-livewire.update` (`POST livewire-3e678b04/update`) carries middleware `web`, `Livewire\Mechanisms\HandleRequests\RequireLivewireHeaders` — the `web` group, not a panel-specific stack. `grep -n -B3 -A3 "EnsureAccountActive" bootstrap/app.php` confirms it is appended to that same `web` group (`bootstrap/app.php:34`). So `EnsureAccountActive` genuinely runs on every Filament panel Livewire-update request — it does not "never" reach the panel.
- `sed -n '95,115p' vendor/filament/filament/src/FilamentServiceProvider.php` confirms `Livewire::addPersistentMiddleware([Authenticate::class, ...])` — Filament's own `Authenticate` (which checks `canAccessPanel()`) is registered as persistent Livewire middleware, independently re-running on panel component updates. This is the real defence-in-depth mechanism for a suspended admin's Livewire actions, not `EnsureAccountActive`'s `admin.` exclusion (which, correctly, never touches the panel's own routes — that much of the original claim was right) and not the `access-admin-area` gate.

**No behavioural change and no invariant at risk** — `canAccessPanel()` and `access-admin-area` both require role Admin + status Active, so a suspended admin is blocked either way; this is a documentation/rationale accuracy correction only. The 23:58 entries and `EnsureAccountActive.php`'s docblock are unedited, per git-history discipline (the docblock is also unedited pending an owner-routed follow-up — see §6 item AB below, not fixed in-cycle per rule 6's code-file bar); this NOTE and PR #35's own REVIEW entry are the correction of record. **Also corrects PR #35's own body**, which repeated the same inaccurate framing implicitly via item (c)'s bullet.

Platform leg is the residual `price − r − t` by `Money` subtraction (zero-sum by construction); document the rounding direction in ADR-021. Leg pattern: escrow −r/refund +r; escrow −t/tutor +t (with `tutor_profile_id`); residual d ≥ 0 → escrow −d/platform +d, d < 0 → escrow +|d|/platform −|d| typed `Goodwill`. ## [2026-09-29 01:41 machine clock] DECISION — trial/no-show dispute defaults: `no_show_tutor` is unreachable as a dispute default; resolved by scenario, not by a new `DisputeReason` value

R150 and PRD §2.10 both state prefill defaults keyed on scenario ("trial lesson", "tutor no-show", "student no-show"), but `DisputeReason` (DATA_MODEL) has a single `no_show` case with no party discriminator, and `MarkNoShow::tutor()` transitions `InProgress -> NoShowTutor -> Refunded` in one transaction (`app/Actions/Lessons/MarkNoShow.php`, read this segment and the one before) — `refunded` is terminal, and a dispute can only open on `completed`/`completed_reported` (R150), so a lesson that reached its no-show automatically via the tutor-no-show path can never reach `disputed` at all. The "tutor no-show -> 100/0" default is therefore unreachable through the system's own automatic detection; it can only describe a manual admin judgement call on a `completed`/`completed_reported` lesson where the account holder disputes with `reason = no_show` and the admin decides, off-record, that the tutor was actually the one who failed to show. Resolution (advisor point 6, this cycle's design consult, adopted verbatim: "map each default to a detectable condition, disclose any unreachable default in §6 rather than inventing a column"): the Filament prefill computes only the two *detectable* defaults — `lesson->type === LessonType::Trial` -> 100/0 (matching PRD's trial text exactly: full refund; tutor pay is `PRD` line 48's "decided separately by admin", so left **empty**, not 0, on a trial — resolving the PRD-vs-R150 wording tension in the PRD's favour per CLAUDE.md's "When unsure" precedence, since PRD is read-only and wins on a PRD/PLAN conflict); `reason === no_show` with no further signal -> both dials left empty, admin must choose (folds correctly into R150's own "otherwise empty" bucket, since student-no-show and tutor-no-show are not distinguishable from stored data alone). No new `DisputeReason` case, no new lesson column added — matches the domain invariant against speculative nullable columns "for later". To be carried into `docs/STATUS.md` §6 as a disclosed plan-repo gap, not fixed by inventing schema.

## [2026-09-29 01:41 machine clock] DECISION — `settle()` reversal-leg design: one new `LedgerEntryType` case (`ReleaseReversal`), reuse existing types for the four SETTLE legs

Empirically confirmed (this segment and the one before, reading `SubmitProgressReport`, `AutoReleaseLesson`, `MarkNoShow::student()`, `CancelLesson::cancelByParent()`'s inside-window branch) that every path into `completed_reported` already writes RELEASE legs (escrow at 0, not price) before or as part of that transition — so DATA_MODEL's SETTLE row ("escrow -price ...") is only directly correct for a dispute opened while still `completed` (escrow untouched, equals price). For a dispute opened on an already-`completed_reported` lesson, `settle()` must first restore escrow to price with typed reversal legs, then apply the unchanged SETTLE legs — both inside one locked transaction, so the combined write still sums to zero (reversal nets to zero on its own; SETTLE legs net to zero on their own: `-price + r + t + (price - r - t) = 0`). Leg design: reversal (only when `balance(Escrow) === 0`, i.e. already released) = `[Escrow, ReleaseReversal, +tutor_amount], [Tutor, ReleaseReversal, -tutor_amount, tutor_profile_id], [Escrow, ReleaseReversal, +commission_amount], [Platform, ReleaseReversal, -commission_amount]`; any `balance(Escrow)` other than `0` or `price` throws (a real ledger inconsistency, not a case to silently handle). SETTLE legs (DATA_MODEL's row, unchanged, read as three independent zero-sum pairs rather than one four-leg line): refund pair `Escrow -r`/`Refund +r`, tutor pair `Escrow -t`/`Tutor +t`, platform pair `Escrow -d`/`Platform +d` (mirrored signs, `Escrow +|d|`/`Platform -|d|`, typed `Goodwill` when `d` is negative) — the three pairs together take `-r-t-d = -price` out of escrow in total, since `d = price-r-t`, matching DATA_MODEL's single "escrow -price" line. No `amount <> 0` constraint exists on `ledger_entries` (confirmed by reading the migration directly, this segment and the one before) — a zero-amount leg (e.g. `t=0` on a `0/100`-inverse dial, or `d=0`) is written anyway rather than special-cased, keeping the leg set uniform and the code simpler; this is deliberately different from `hold()`'s and `release()`'s existing all-nonzero legs, disclosed here rather than silently assumed. To be recorded in ADR-021 alongside the rounding direction (`Money::percentage()`, half-up on fils, same primitive PRD's own dial percentages call for — not `splitCommission()`, which is specific to the price/commission booking-time split and rounds tutor-down deliberately for a different invariant).

Two real bugs found and fixed while building `tests/Feature/Lessons/OpenDisputeTest.php` (16 new
tests, all failing-before/passing-after their own fix, not pre-existing coverage):

1. **`OpenDispute.php`** — `Dispute::query()->create([...])` never set `status` (deliberately not
   `$fillable`: it is set once, only by the DB's own default `DisputeStatus::Open`, never chosen by
   the caller), so the returned in-memory model's `status` attribute was simply unset — `null`, not
   `DisputeStatus::Open` — since Eloquent's `create()` does not re-read the row after an insert.
   Fixed with an explicit `$dispute->refresh()` right after `create()`. Caught by the "right up to
   the 48h edge" happy-path test asserting `$dispute->status->value === 'open'`.
2. **`tests/Feature/Lessons/OpenDisputeTest.php`**, in `disputeSetup()` — a `static $slot` offset
   (`+= 120` minutes per call), added defensively against a scheduling collision that cannot
   actually happen here (each call gets its own fresh `TutorProfile`/`Learner`; grepped every
   `unique(` in `database/migrations` and confirmed no index keys lessons on time alone), was being
   added on top of `now()->subMinutes($minutesAgo)` for `starts_at`/`ends_at`/`completed_at`. That
   shifted `ends_at` away from `now()` by the same amount, silently corrupting the precise
   "$hoursAgo since real now()" the 48h-boundary tests depend on — the "48h and 1 minute after
   ends_at" dataset case ended up only ~36h stale (well inside the window), so `problemFor()`

## [2026-09-29 03:04 machine clock] NOTE — auto-release/late-strike safety confirmed, dropdown label fixed, no new test needed

Two safety properties the advisor asked to have checked against the code, not just asserted, both
confirmed clean:

1. **The auto-release sweep already excludes a disputed lesson.** `AutoReleaseLesson::due()`
   (`app/Actions/Lessons/AutoReleaseLesson.php:57-67`) queries only `where('status', LessonStatus::Completed)`
   — a `disputed` lesson never matches. Even in a race (a dispute opens between the sweep's query and
   its per-lesson lock), `LessonStateMachine::transition($lesson, LessonStatus::CompletedReported, ...)`
   has no `disputed -> completed_reported` edge, throws `LessonTransitionException`, and
   `AutoReleaseReports::handle()` (`app/Console/Commands/AutoReleaseReports.php:29-38`) catches that
   exception per-lesson and moves on without releasing.
2. **Disputing can never cause a false late-report strike.** `report_late_at` (the sole input to
   `ReviewLateReports`'s strike count) is written only by `AutoReleaseLesson.php:36`, only when an
   auto-release actually completes — which point 1 shows a disputed lesson can never reach. A parent
   disputing a lesson can only ever prevent a late flag, never cause one.

**Correcting the advisor's own "the hold has no test" claim (its point 3a from the pre-compaction
consult):** it is wrong. `tests/Feature/Lessons/AutoReleaseReportsTest.php:144-162`

`auto_release_at`, runs the sweep, and asserts the lesson's status is still `disputed`,
`report_late_at` stays null, no ledger entries change, and the command exits successfully — exactly
the coverage the advisor described as missing. Re-ran it standalone this segment:

L3: lesson 3, dispute 3, status settled, sum 0 fils

- **L1** (100/0): `refund = Money::fils(10000)->percentage(100) = 10000`, `tutor =
  Money::fils(7500)->percentage(0) = 0`, `platformDelta = 10000-10000-0 = 0` → only a `refund` leg
  pair (escrow -10000 / refund +10000) after the `hold` pair. No `release_tutor`/commission legs,
  matching a 0-value leg being skipped (`if ($tutor !== 0)`, `if ($platformDelta !== 0)`).
- **L2** (0/100): `refund = 0`, `tutor = Money::fils(7500)->percentage(100) = 7500`, `platformDelta
  = 10000-0-7500 = 2500` → `release_tutor` pair (7500) + `release_commission` pair (2500, positive
  ⇒ `ReleaseCommission` type per `$platformDelta < 0 ? Goodwill : ReleaseCommission`), no refund leg.
- **L3** (trial, 100/0): identical shape to L1 scaled to price 8000 — refund 8000 only.
- **L4** (33/67, already-released): `escrow === 0` at settle time (confirmed: prior `release()`

  `ReleaseCommission`, the platform's cut of the settlement, distinct from the reversed original
  commission). All 3 leg pairs sum with the 2 reversal pairs and the original hold/release pairs to
  exactly 0 across the lesson's 14 `ledger_entries` rows.

[2026-09-29 08:13] DECISION — CC: ForceCompleteLesson anchors report_due_at/auto_release_at on now(), not ends_at
Read app/Console/Commands/AutoReleaseReports.php and AutoReleaseLesson::due(): the sweep trusts the
frozen auto_release_at column on the row (falls back to ends_at+hours only for legacy rows where that
column is null) — whatever ForceCompleteLesson writes to the row governs the sweep, confirmed, not
assumed. Read AutoReleaseLesson::__invoke(): it stamps report_late_at unconditionally the moment
escrow auto-releases, with no check on whether the deadline had already been in the past when the
lesson became completed. Read ReviewLateReports: 3 lessons with report_late_at set inside a rolling
90-day window auto-creates a late_report_x3 TutorStrike row and emails admins. Chain: if
ForceCompleteLesson anchored on the literal ends_at for a lesson stuck days past its scheduled end,
auto_release_at = ends_at + auto_release_hours would already be in the past the instant the transition
commits — the very next 5-minute sweep run would immediately release escrow and stamp report_late_at,
for a delay the admin (or a Daily webhook failure) caused, not the tutor, with no way to distinguish it
from a genuine late report. Decision: anchor both report_due_at and auto_release_at on now() at the
moment of the forced completed transition, reading report_due_hours/auto_release_hours from Settings
exactly as SettleEndedLesson::complete() already does — frozen on the row the same way, invariant 11
intact (the window lengths are still the settings-driven, frozen-on-the-lesson values; only the anchor
instant differs from the ordinary on-time path). Consistent with R151's "then the normal release path —
report or 72h auto-release, unchanged": the mechanism is unchanged, only the instant a genuinely-late
completion is judged from moves to the instant an admin actually closed it out.

[2026-09-29 08:13] DECISION — CC: ForceCompleteLesson requires ends_at to already be in the past, both in_progress and confirmed
Mirrors SettleEndedLesson::complete()'s own guard (ends_at->isFuture() refuses). Nothing gets
force-completed mid-session; an admin cannot end a lesson that is still scheduled to be running.
confirmed -> in_progress -> completed and the direct in_progress -> completed edge both carry this
same check inside the one DB::transaction.

[2026-09-29 08:13] DECISION — CC: OpenDispute's 48h ends_at-anchored window is left untouched this sub-cycle; disclosed, not fixed
A lesson force-completed more than 48h after its own ends_at would find OpenDispute::problemFor()
already refusing the moment it becomes disputable, leaving the affected family no real recourse if the
forced completion was wrong. OpenDispute is merged 9b money code, not named in R151's scope, and
changing its anchor (e.g. to completed_at) is a real design change to already-shipped, tested behaviour
that deserves its own review, not a drive-by edit inside 9c. Recorded in S6 (new item, see STATUS.md
rewrite) with a recommended Owner action; does not block 9c's build — the scenario requires a lesson to
have been stuck uncompleted for 46+ hours before an admin acts, the same rare-and-already-disclosed
shape as item 0b/0c(a).

[2026-09-29 08:13] DECISION — CC: force-complete's unmasking of conversation contact details on a single-party-joined lesson is accepted admin-judgment design, not a gap
SyncConversationForLesson stamps first_lesson_completed_at (invariant 8's masking gate) unconditionally
on any transition to Completed, with no check on tutor_joined_at/learner_joined_at. Force-complete's
whole purpose (S6 0b, 0c(a)) is the case where the ordinary SettleEndedLesson::complete() never ran
because it requires both join timestamps non-null — so a force-completed lesson may genuinely have only
one side's join timestamp set, or neither. The admin's required note is the safety mechanism here, the
same trust-the-admin-with-an-audited-note pattern MarkProviderFailure already uses for an equally
consequential call. Decision: no extra join-state guard is added — an admin marking a lesson complete
is asserting, on the record, that it happened. Disclosed in S6 for the reviewer's attention, not
treated as a defect.

[2026-09-29 08:13] DECISION — CC: cancel_reason for ForceCancelLesson is the new machine value LessonCancelReason::Admin ('admin'), not a copied user-typed note
R151's own text names the reason literally as admin. LessonCancelReason's docblock scopes the enum to
machine-readable values written to cancel_reason when the platform, not a person's typed note, cancels
a lesson — matches an admin panel action, not a tutor/parent's own free-text cancel (CancelLesson,
which writes the raw string with no enum involved). Using a fixed enum value rather than the admin's
free-text note also sidesteps isReserved()'s existing collision guard entirely. The admin's required
note goes into the audit log's payload only (RecordAuditLog's $after), mirroring MarkProviderFailure's
exact convention — never onto the lesson row. Confirmed side effect, not a defect: the recurring
(recurring_slot_id, starts_at) partial unique index frees a row's key only for cancel_reason =
'slot_paused'; 'admin' is not that value, so a force-cancelled recurring-generated lesson keeps its key
and recurring:generate cannot recreate it next run — the same protective behaviour TutorSuspended/
AccountSuspended already rely on, to be pinned by a test.

[2026-09-29 08:13] DECISION — CC: notification behaviour for ForceCancelLesson — silent for reserved, existing generic mail/bell kept (with a copy fix) for confirmed
Because LessonCancelReason::Admin will make isReserved($lesson->cancel_reason) true: (1) a reserved
force-cancel gets no mail (SendLessonSkippedMail returns early on any recognised machine value) and no
bell (RecordLessonCancelledNotification's freeSkip branch is gated the same way) — total silence, the
same deliberate-silence shape already established for TutorSuspended/AccountSuspended/SlotPaused/
SlotEnded. Decision: accept this silence for v1 rather than build a new dedicated mail/notification
pair R151 never asked for (CLAUDE.md's scope guard) — disclosed in S6, not silently assumed. (2) A
confirmed force-cancel is unaffected on the send/no-send side — both mail and bell fire as they already
do for a normal cancellation, gated only on from=Confirmed && to=Cancelled, not on cancel_reason. Real
problem found: cancelled.blade.php prints cancel_reason raw with no guard ("Reason given:
{{ $lesson->cancel_reason }}"), so a confirmed force-cancel would literally show the family and tutor
the string "Reason given: admin" — an internal machine value leaking as customer-facing copy. Fix: guard
the blade view the same way SendLessonSkippedMail already guards its own send — skip the "Reason given"
line when LessonCancelReason::isReserved($lesson->cancel_reason) is true — so any current or future
machine value is silently omitted while a genuine tutor/parent-typed reason still shows as it does
today. Confirmed SendWeeklyChargeMails.php:34's own CancelledByTutor branch checks cancel_reason ===
TutorUnavailable->value specifically, so 'admin' cannot trigger its wrong copy there — no fix needed.
